claim: Fedora Linux 44 shipped 28 April 2026 with kernel 6.19, GNOME 50, Plasma 6.6, and Atomic Desktop variants alongside the traditional editions.
quote: Release Date: April 28, 2026. Kernel Version: 6.19.14-300.fc44. GNOME 50 (Workstation), Plasma 6.6 (KDE Plasma Desktop). Atomic Desktop variants (Silverblue, Kinoite, Cosmic, Budgie, Sway) and alternate spins are also available.

claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon' ships Linux 7.0, a Wayland-only GNOME session, Rust-based sudo-rs and uutils coreutils, TPM-backed full-disk encryption, and CUDA/ROCm in the archive.
quote: Linux 7.0 kernel at release... Rust-based system components (kernel drivers, sudo-rs, uutils coreutils)... TPM-backed full-disk encryption now generally available... natively distribute NVIDIA CUDA as part of its software repositories

claim: Debian 13 'trixie' is current stable at point release 13.6 (11 July 2026); testing is 'forky'; each stable gets three years of full support plus two years of LTS.
quote: Version 13, codenamed "Trixie," released August 9, 2025. The latest point release is 13.6 (July 11, 2026). Testing distribution is codenamed "Forky"... five years: the first three years of full support followed by two years of Long Term Support (LTS).

claim: Bluefin's Spring 2026 release rebases on Fedora 44 and moves from rpm-ostree to bootc with sealed images, composefs, UKI and systemd-boot; its developer story is devcontainers, Homebrew and Distrobox.
quote: Bluefin Spring 2026 runs on Fedora 44 with GNOME 50... transitioning from rpm-ostree to bootc with sealed base images featuring composefs, UKI (Unified Kernel Images), and verified boot chains... emphasizes containerized development through devcontainers, Homebrew, and Distrobox

claim: DistroWatch's April 2026 hits-per-day ranking put CachyOS first, Linux Mint second and MX Linux third.
quote: According to DistroWatch's hits-per-day metric, the three most popular distributions in April 2026 were: 1. CachyOS 2. Linux Mint 3. MX Linux

claim: Ubuntu releases every six months, LTS every two years with five years of standard security maintenance, extendable to ten via Ubuntu Pro ESM and fifteen with the Legacy add-on; interim releases get nine months.
quote: Ubuntu releases a new version every six months... Long-Term Support versions arrive every two years and provide 5 years of standard security maintenance... Years 6-10: Expanded Security Maintenance (ESM) via Ubuntu Pro; Years 11-15: Legacy add-on

claim: Fedora is governed by the Fedora Council, FESCo and Mindshare with Red Hat as primary sponsor; releases land roughly every six months and are supported about 13 months; Fedora is upstream of CentOS Stream and RHEL.
quote: Fedora operates through a community-driven model led by the Fedora Council... Red Hat provides primary sponsorship... version X is supported only until 1 month after version X+2 is released... Fedora serves as the upstream source for both CentOS Stream and Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

claim: Arch is a rolling release with pacman and the community-run AUR, led by Levente Polyak on two-year terms, with Valve funding build and signing infrastructure since September 2024.
quote: In September 2024, Valve Corporation partnered with Arch Linux developers to support ongoing efforts, focusing on "build service infrastructure and secure signing enclave."... Arch Linux employs a rolling release approach without scheduled version numbers.

claim: On 12 June 2026 Arch announced an active AUR incident of malicious package adoptions and updates, telling users to review every PKGBUILD and install-script change.
quote: a high volume of malicious package adoptions and updates... review _all_ PKGBUILD and install script changes when updating, especially during this time.

claim: More than 1,500 AUR packages were affected; Arch published a list of 1,579 compromised packages and believed the incident contained.
quote: The incident impacted over 1,500 user-contributed packages... a list documenting 1,579 compromised packages, though this was described as a "list containing many (but not all) of the affected packages"

claim: The June 2026 'Atomic Arch' campaign hijacked orphaned AUR packages to deploy an infostealer and an eBPF rootkit that exfiltrated credentials, tokens and SSH keys.
quote: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR Packages Hijacked to Deploy Infostealer and eBPF Rootkit

claim: CachyOS is a community-run Arch derivative that rebuilds kernel and packages for x86-64-v3/v4 and Zen 4 with BORE scheduling, ships a Calamares installer and monthly ISOs, and overtook Arch in ProtonDB reports in March 2026.
quote: rebuilds its kernel and core packages with CPU-architecture-specific compiler optimizations targeting x86-64-v3 and x86-64-v4 microarchitecture levels, plus AMD Zen 4 support... March 2026: Surpassed Arch Linux in ProtonDB game-compatibility reports

claim: DistroWatch's ranking counts page hits, not installs or usage share, so it signals interest rather than adoption.
quote: DistroWatch's hit-counter statistics measure page visits rather than installation numbers or usage share, and cautioned against treating the ranking as a definitive popularity measure

claim: Linux Mint 22.3 'Zena' (January 2026) is based on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with Cinnamon 6.6 and is supported to April 2029.
quote: Linux Mint 22.3 "Zena" Released, Based on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS

claim: Mint's next major release is not expected until around December 2026, a deliberate move to a longer development cycle.
quote: Linux Mint's next release won't be until Christmas 2026

claim: Linux Mint 23 is being built on the Ubuntu 26.04 LTS base with the Linux 7.0 kernel and Wayland work.
quote: Linux Mint 23 Making Progress On Ubuntu 26.04 Base, Linux 7.0 Kernel & Wayland

claim: In Mint 23 Wayland stops being experimental and becomes a fully supported option, but X11 remains the default session.
quote: Linux Mint says Wayland support in its next release will no longer be considered experimental, but available as a fully-supported option.

claim: Zorin OS 18.1 (April 2026) sits on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS with the 6.17 HWE kernel and arrived after ~3.3 million downloads of 18.x, adding an Xfce-based Lite edition.
quote: Zorin OS 18.1 released - and the Lite edition reappears... arriving six months and some 3.3 million downloads after the original launch

claim: COSMIC is System76's Rust desktop; Epoch 1 shipped 11 December 2025 and point releases continued through 1.0.13 in May 2026.
quote: COSMIC is a free and open-source desktop environment for Linux... originally released August 5, 2024, with the stable release 1.0.13 released May 12, 2026.

claim: Rocky Linux targets bug-for-bug 1:1 binary compatibility with RHEL, while AlmaLinux builds from CentOS Stream for ABI compatibility and can diverge to keep older hardware working.
quote: AlmaLinux targets ABI compatibility with RHEL and can patch ahead of strict clone parity; Rocky Linux aims for 1:1 binary compatibility with RHEL.

claim: openSUSE Leap 16 is the family's first major rebase since 2018: SELinux replaces AppArmor, YaST is retired from the GUI in favour of the Agama installer plus Cockpit and Myrlyn, kernel 6.12, support to 2031.
quote: SELinux has replaced AppArmor as the default mandatory access control (MAC) system... The new Agama installer provides a streamlined experience... two years per point release rather than 18 months, with overall support extending through 2031.

claim: openSUSE offers Leap (point releases sharing SUSE Linux Enterprise sources), Tumbleweed (rolling from Factory after openQA gating) and Slowroll (Tumbleweed on a slower monthly cadence).
quote: Tumbleweed pushes out updates continuously from the rolling development repository Factory after packages have passed automated testing... Slowroll is a rolling-release distribution that aims to provide more stability than Tumbleweed by sending out monthly updates

claim: openSUSE Aeon is the immutable GNOME desktop built on Tumbleweed and is still at release-candidate stage; the KDE counterpart Kalpa remains early-stage.
quote: Aeon Desktop is an independent immutable operating system based on openSUSE Tumbleweed... The distro is still in a Release Candidate stage.

claim: NixOS 26.05 'Yarara' released 30 May 2026 with a seven-month support window, GNOME 50, and 59,703 commits from 2,842 contributors.
quote: The 26.05 release was made possible due to the efforts of 2842 contributors, who authored 59703 commits since the previous release... receives bugfixes and security updates for seven months, ending December 31, 2026.

claim: nixpkgs is the single monorepo behind NixOS and the Nix package set.
quote: Nix Packages collection & NixOS

claim: Fedora ships five Atomic Desktop variants — Silverblue (GNOME), Kinoite (KDE), Sway, Budgie and COSMIC — with an image-based, versioned base system.
quote: Silverblue - an atomic GNOME-based desktop aimed at good support for container-focused workflows... Kinoite... Sway Atomic... Budgie Atomic... COSMIC Atomic

claim: Bluefin is Universal Blue's GNOME workstation image, positioned as a reliability-focused Linux workstation.
quote: The next generation Linux workstation, designed for reliability, performance, and sustainability.

claim: Aurora is Universal Blue's KDE Plasma image, the atomic counterpart to Bluefin.
quote: Aurora features a lightly customized KDE Plasma 6 desktop experience

claim: Community complaints about atomic desktops centre on developer tooling: IDEs, sdkman/pyenv and Oracle client libraries are awkward to install, documentation gaps bite when something breaks, and Distrobox is reported as unreliable.
quote: installing necessary tools like "IntelliJ, Pycharm, sdkman, pyenv, Oracle libraries and binaries, databases, etc." presented significant obstacles... distrobox... is "simply broken"

claim: Docker Engine is officially supported and tested on Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, RHEL and CentOS only; derivatives are untested and Arch/openSUSE are not listed.
quote: Docker doesn't test or verify installation on distribution derivatives.

claim: .NET 10's commercially supported Linux matrix is Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, Fedora, openSUSE Leap, Alpine and CentOS Stream — Arch and its derivatives are absent.
quote: .NET 10 supports Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, Debian 11 and 12, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.10, 9.7, and 10.1, Fedora 39 and 40, openSUSE Leap 15.5+, Alpine Linux 3.18+, and CentOS Stream 9.

claim: Fedora installs the proprietary NVIDIA driver under Secure Boot by generating a local key with mokutil and prompting the user to enrol it on reboot.
quote: Fedora uses mokutil to create a key for users to self-sign drivers, asking for a password during installation, and presenting the mokutil interface to enroll the key on reboot.

claim: Debian elected Sruthi Chandran as Project Leader in April 2026, 289 votes to 50 for 'None of the above', with the term starting 21 April 2026.
quote: Chandran won decisively with 289 votes compared to 50 votes for "None of the above"... New term begins: April 21, 2026

claim: Debian has no corporate owner: Software in the Public Interest holds its assets in trust and donations are administered by the Project Leader.
quote: Software in the Public Interest is a non-profit organization that holds assets in trust for Debian. Donations are managed by the Debian Project Leader (DPL)

claim: Manjaro holds Arch packages back, which desynchronises its repositories from the AUR and causes AUR builds to fail against older dependencies.
quote: some AUR packages require certain dependencies from the official Arch repo, but on Manjaro the necessary dependency might be running on an older version with compatibility issues

claim: EndeavourOS is a thin graphical installer over upstream Arch: official Arch repositories, minimal defaults, aimed at hands-on intermediate users.
quote: EndeavourOS deliberately stays minimal and close to upstream Arch. It uses the official Arch repositories and ships with sensible defaults rather than opinionated configurations.

claim: StatCounter put desktop Linux at 2.99% in April 2026, a figure depressed by an 'Unknown' bucket that has grown to 16.77%.
quote: StatCounter's April 2026 monthly reading sits lower at 2.99%, pulled down by an Unknown category that has swelled to 16.77%.

claim: Debian 13 trixie ships the Linux 6.12 LTS kernel series.
quote: Debian 13 Trixie is powered by the long-term supported Linux 6.12 LTS kernel series.

claim: Mint ships Flatpak and removed Snap support outright over disagreements with Canonical's single-vendor store and closed server protocol.
quote: The Snap client is designed to work with only one source, following a protocol which isn't open, and using only one authentication system.

claim: A 2026 developer-focused survey recommends Fedora Workstation as the default developer distro and Ubuntu LTS where maximum compatibility and minimum tweaking matter.
quote: For most developers, most of the time, Fedora Workstation is recommended, while Ubuntu LTS is suggested for those who want maximum compatibility and minimum tweaking.
